claim_1.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from seven Ad5 nAb seronegative individuals during the first week after vaccination, using gene-level analysis of Affymetrix exon microarrays with false-discovery rate (FDR) ≤10% and absolute average log2 fold-change ≥0.5, showed that responses to MRKAd5/HIV peaked at 24 h compared to prevaccination across the candidate set of prevaccination, 24 h, 72 h, and 168 h postvaccination.

sources.quote: Responses to MRKAd5/HIV peaked at 24 h, with 1,026 genes exhibiting enhanced and 1,048 genes exhibiting re- pressed expression levels compared with prevaccination (Fig. 1A and Dataset S1, tab 1).

(A) In vivo PBMC transcriptional responses to vaccination with MRKAd5/HIV [n = 7 Ad5 seronegative individuals, false-discovery rate (FDR) ≤10%, absolute average log2 fold-change ≥0.5]. Genes signiﬁcantly differentially expressed in response to MRKAd5/HIV vaccination at any time point are annotated and grouped according to membership in functional gene modules (21, 64). Each column represents subject-speciﬁc log2(fold-changes) compared with prevaccination. To emphasize regulation patterns, expression fold-changes for each gene are scaled by the maximum observed expression response. Pink intensity indicates up- regulation compared with prevaccination, cyan indicates down-regulation.

sources.quote: No signiﬁcantly differentially expressed genes were detected at 168 h.

claim_4.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from seven Ad5 nAb seronegative individuals during the first week after vaccination, using a modular analysis framework with false-discovery rate (FDR) <10% and |average log2(fold-change)|>0.5, showed that the modular response peaked at 24 h compared to prevaccination across the candidate set of prevaccination, 24 h, 72 h, and 168 h postvaccination.

sources.quote: Mirroring the gene-level results, the modular response peaked at 24 h (13 up-regulated and 11 down-regulated modules), waned by 72 h (two up-regulated modules), and returned to baseline by 168 h (Fig. 1B).

(B) Functional gene modules signiﬁcantly differentially expressed in PBMC in response to vaccination. Each black line represents the average log2(fold change) of all genes in the module for a single subject. Up-regulated modules have values >0, down-regulated modules have values <0. FDR < 10%, |average log2(fold-change)|>0.5.

claim_7.claim: qRT-PCR analysis of PBMC from seven vaccinated individuals during the first week after MRKAd5/HIV vaccination, using transcript quantification for quantitative RT-PCR validation of module-associated genes identified by microarray analysis, showed differential expression of CXCL10, ISG-15, and STAT1 compared to prevaccination.

sources.quote: First, we quantiﬁed and conﬁrmed the dif- ferential expression of mRNAs associated with several vaccine- regulated modules, including “Interferon response” [C-X-C motif chemokine 10 (CXCL10), ISG-15, and STAT1] (Fig. 1C).
(C) Quantitative RT-PCR validation of the differential expression of module-associated genes identiﬁed by microarray analysis. Each line represents the response of one individual (n = 7).

claim_8.claim: Luminex analysis of serum from vaccinated subjects after MRKAd5/HIV, using multiplex analyte analysis for protein-level validation of vaccine-induced cytokine and chemokine differential expression, showed robust changes in IP-10, I-TAC, MCP-1, MCP-2, IL-10, and IL-1Ra compared to prevaccination.

sources.quote: Next, we corroborated the differential expression of many cytokines and chemokines at the protein level using multiplex serum analyte analysis (Fig. 1D and Dataset S1, tab 6), detecting robust changes in serum levels of IP-10, I-TAC, monocyte chemo- attractant protein-1 (MCP-1), and MCP-2, as well as immuno- regulatory IL-10 and IL-1Ra.
(D) Protein-level validation of vaccine- induced cytokine and chemokine differential expression by multiplex analyte analysis.

claim_9.claim: flow cytometry analysis of whole blood from vaccinated subjects after MRKAd5/HIV, using a statistical model assessing change in concentration over time with Hochberg adjustment, showed vaccine-induced influx of monocytes compared to prevaccination.

sources.quote: Finally, we validated the cellular trafﬁcking responses predicted from the modular analysis by directly assessing circulating peripheral blood leukocyte con- centrations (Fig. 1E and Dataset S1, tab 7), conﬁrming vaccine- induced inﬂux of monocytes and pronounced efﬂux of lympho- cyte populations (T, B, and NK cells).

(E) Validation of vaccine-induced cellular ﬂuxes predicted by module-level analysis of the PBMC transcriptional responses. *P < 0.05 with Hochberg adjustment from the statistical model assessing change in concentration over time.

claim_11.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from vaccinated Ad5 seropositive subjects compared to subjects with Ad5 nAb titers ≤200, using in vivo innate immune response profiling, showed that vaccine-induced responses of 306 seropositivity effect genes were markedly attenuated in subjects with Ad5 nAb titers >200.

sources.quote: Given the possibility of threshold effects of Ad5 nAb (3, 4), we compared the responses between subjects with Ad5 nAb titers ≤200 and >200, and thereby identiﬁed 306 seropositivity effect genes (302 at 24 h, six at 72 h) for which the vaccine-induced responses were markedly attenuated (Dataset S1, tab 11).

claim_12.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from vaccinated Ad5 seropositive subjects compared to subjects with Ad5 nAb titers ≤200, using canonical pathway enrichment analysis of the 306 seropositivity effect genes, showed that induction of complement pathways, innate immune sensors, and G-protein coupled receptor signaling was significantly attenuated in subjects with Ad5 nAb titers >200.

sources.quote: Canonical pathway enrichment analysis of these genes revealed that induction of complement pathways, innate immune sensors, and G-protein coupled receptor signaling was signiﬁcantly attenuated (Dataset S1, tab 12).

claim_13.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from vaccinated Ad5 seropositive subjects compared to subjects with Ad5 nAb titers ≤200, using modular analysis, showed that attenuation extended to all modules regulated by the MRKAd5 vaccine in subjects with Ad5 nAb titers >200.

sources.quote: This attenuation extended to all modules regulated by the MRKAd5 vaccine (Fig. 3A), including impaired down-regula- tion of lymphocyte modules and genes preferentially expressed in lymphocytes (Dataset S1, tab 11), suggesting suppression of the acute lymphopenia observed in the Ad5 seronegative subjects (Fig. 1E).

claim_14.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from vaccinated Ad5 seropositive subjects compared to subjects with Ad5 nAb titers ≤200, using modular analysis, showed impaired down-regulation of lymphocyte modules and genes preferentially expressed in lymphocytes in subjects with Ad5 nAb titers >200.

sources.quote: This attenuation extended to all modules regulated by the MRKAd5 vaccine (Fig. 3A), including impaired down-regula- tion of lymphocyte modules and genes preferentially expressed in lymphocytes (Dataset S1, tab 11), suggesting suppression of the acute lymphopenia observed in the Ad5 seronegative subjects (Fig. 1E).

claim_15.claim: Luminex analysis of serum from vaccinated subjects compared between subjects with Ad5 nAb titers >200 and subjects with Ad5 nAb titers ≤200 showed that cytokine responses were markedly attenuated in subjects with Ad5 nAb titers >200.

sources.quote: Consistent with the transcriptional results, cytokine responses were markedly attenuated in Ad5 nAb >200 subjects compared with Ad5 nAb ≤200 subjects (Fig. 3C and Dataset S1, tab 13).

claim_16.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from subjects with high and low CD8+ T-cell response groups after MRKAd5/HIV, using direct comparison of vaccine-induced transcriptional responses, showed that significant differences between the groups were identified only at 72 h postvaccination.

sources.quote: Surprisingly, signiﬁcant differences between these groups of sub- jects were only identiﬁed from the transcriptional responses measured 72 h postvaccination (88 genes were positively associ- ated and 121 genes were negatively associated) (Fig. 5 A and B and Dataset S1, tab 14), and none of the MRKAd5-responsive mod- ules differed signiﬁcantly between the groups.

claim_50.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from 7 healthy HIV-1-uninfected adults over prevaccination and 6, 24, 72, and 168 h after MRKAd5/HIV vaccination, using comparative transcriptomic analysis against published YF-17D in vivo profiles, showed that MRKAd5/HIV induced a greater number of significantly up-regulated and down-regulated innate immune genes than YF-17D compared to prevaccination.

sources.quote: Replication-Incompetent MRKAd5 Induces a Greater Number of Innate Immune Genes than Does Live-Attenuated YF-17D, but the Response Is More Transient.
Although the MRKAd5/HIV vaccine induced more than 1,000 genes and repressed a similar number, the YF-17D vaccine only induced 181 genes and repressed 10 genes (Fig. 6A).

(A) MRKAd5/HIV and YF-17D trigger innate immune responses in PBMC with distinct kinetics in vivo. The number of genes signiﬁcantly up-regulated (upper half) or down-regulated (lower half) in response to vaccination with MRKAd5/HIV (red, present study) or YF-17D [blue (19)] are plotted. Signiﬁcant differential expression deﬁned as FDR ≤10%, | average[log2(fold-change)]| > 0.5; n = 7 (MRKAd5/HIV), n = 25 (YF-17D).

claim_53.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from four Ad5 seronegative donors stimulated in vitro for 24 h, using comparative in vivo and in vitro transcriptomic analysis, showed that 43 genes were preferentially induced by MRKAd5 and confirmed in vivo and in vitro compared to controls and compared to YF-17D.

sources.quote: We identified 43 genes preferentially induced by MRKAd5/HIV in vivo that confirmed in vitro (Fig. 6C), including several associated with innate immune responses (IRF1), the complement pathway (C1QB), pathogen recognition (TLR8), the inflammasome (CASP10, P2RX7), and NK-cell activation [SLAMF7 (33)].

(C) Average expression responses in vivo and in vitro of 43 genes preferentially induced by MRKAd5. Genes associated with functional gene modules are indicated. Rows are scaled as in Fig. 1A. Pink intensity indicates up-regulation compared with controls, cyan indicates down-regulation. FDR < 10%, |average log2(fold-change)|>0.5 for induction in response to MRKAd5 and comparing MRKAd5 to YF- 17D, in vivo and in vitro.

claim_56.claim: microarray analysis of PBMC from four Ad5 seronegative donors stimulated in vitro for 24 h, using comparative in vivo and in vitro transcriptomic analysis, showed that IRF1, KLF4, and STAT5A were preferentially induced by MRKAd5 in vivo and in vitro compared to controls and compared to YF-17D.

sources.quote: The preferential induction of three transcription factors by MRKAd5, IRF1, KLF4, and STAT5A suggested that these factors may partly account for the PBMC transcriptome induced by MRKAd5.

(D) Putative transcriptional regulatory network controlling innate immune responses preferentially induced by MRKAd5. Squares indicate transcription factors preferentially induced by MRKAd5 in vivo and in vitro; circles indicate target genes preferentially induced (pink) or repressed (light blue) by MRKAd5 in vivo and in vitro. Lines indicate protein-DNA transcription factor–target gene interactions identiﬁed from published ChIP-seq datasets [blue, KLF4 targets (38); purple, IRF1 targets (37); orange, STAT5A targets (39)]. Pink edges indicate IRF1 target genes identiﬁed by conventional methods (66–68).
